Samir — thanks, that’s clear. I’m attaching a concise benchmarking appendix and an outline of acceptance criteria we typically include in MAPs. High level notes up front:

- We validated long-context behavior up to 65k seq (65,536 tokens) using continuous KV-cache testing and synthetic prompt distributions derived from your sample payloads.
- Summary numbers (see attached CSV for full run): P50 latency = 58ms (seq 512 median prompt), P95 = 210ms, P99 = 380ms. TTFT median = 85ms. Throughput (tokens/sec) varies by sequence length: ~120k t/s at seq 256, ~36k t/s at seq 2k when batching allowed.
- Concurrency: stable at 128 concurrent streams for steady-state generation at seq<=512. We observed tail-sensitivity above 64 concur for >4k sequences without aggressive batching.
- KV-cache impact: repeated prompt prefixes reduce per-token compute by ~28-35% in our runs; prefix-heavy workloads show biggest gains.

Action items we need from EdgeApps to finalize acceptance criteria in the MAP:
1) Confirm the 95th-percentile TTFT SLA you need for live traffic (we proposed 200ms).
2) Confirm the operational concurrency range (your spike tolerance).
3) Approve the benchmarking data snapshot we put in the appendix for procurement.

I’ll also propose a short gating checklist for go/no-go in this email thread. Marissa — looping you for commercial/credits approval note. Vivek/Neha — please confirm the test artifacts attached and any caveats to highlight (quantization, model family).

Thanks,
Olga

Attachments:
- benchmark-run-20261128.csv (summary + per-run traces)
- kvcache-impact-summary.pdf (3-pg methodology & results)

Samir / team — quick technical addendum from the engineer who ran the experiments:

Test matrix summary (selected rows):
- Model variant: rwd-llamax-70b-int8 (quantized path)
- Sequence lengths tested: 256, 512, 2k, 8k, 32k, 65k (end-to-end generation with KV cache warm and cold scenarios)
- Prompt distribution: 60% short chat-style (<=512 tokens), 30% medium (512-2k), 10% long-context (>2k) — matches EdgeApps sample.
- Concurrency envelope: runs at 16, 32, 64, 128 concurrent streams.

Select results (median of 3 runs):
- Seq 256, concurrency 64: P50 latency 52ms, P95 180ms, P99 300ms, TTFT 78ms, throughput ~125k t/s
- Seq 2k, concurrency 32: P50 latency 160ms, P95 420ms, P99 720ms, TTFT 160ms, throughput ~48k t/s
- Seq 32k, concurrency 8: average generation sustained, P50 1.8s per token-window (note: token-window effects for very long seqs), KV-cache warm reduced compute by ~33% vs cold start
- Seq 65k, concurrency 2: end-to-end stability validated, but higher tail variance observed; recommend limiting single-request max to 65k with per-request timeout of 120s for production call paths.

Caveats / operational notes:
- Quantized 8-bit path gives significant throughput gains but increases P99 variance for very long sequences; we recommend enabling mixed-precision fallback for mission-critical low-tail workloads.
- Batching helps throughput but increases TTFT; for latency-sensitive flows we suggest smaller batch targets and a KV-cache-first routing policy.

I’ve attached the raw CSV and the KV-cache summary. If these numbers look good to you, we can bake the acceptance thresholds into the MAP. Proposed acceptance thresholds: P95 latency <= 350ms for typical production prompt distribution, TTFT median <= 200ms, stability under 64 concurrent streams.

Vivek
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
